rv.q: Axelle Fanyo’s Tosca offers more flair, with an exciting high register, but her good intentions are hampered by an uneven vocal line.
This is not, I'm afraid, a vintage Tosca – but Purves's Scarpia just might be.

Grammy-winning soprano Axelle Fanyo's spirited Tosca, as sexy as any Bond girl, hits the high notes in her ENO debut. Most memorable is her powerful aria "Vissi d'arte", with reflections on life, faith and dedication to art while placed in difficult circumstances.
Annilese Miskimmon's new staging is the sixth I've encountered at the Coliseum, and easily the worst.

Looking for accessible storytelling, spectacle and excellent opera: Look no further than ENO’s fresh new production of this oft-performed classic. The English National Opera’s new production of TOSCA by Puccini (Rome, 1900) of Amanda Holden’s translation, is directed by Annilese Miskimmon, Artistic Director of the ENO.
The standout performance comes from the ENO orchestra under Ben Glassberg, who embody every ounce of the majesty of Puccini's score.

cn.t: Mixed reception for ENO's contemporary Tosca, with critics divided on the updated staging. Praised for thrilling moments and strong conducting, but criticized for uneven casting and a misconceived dramatic approach that undermines Act Two's impact.
